paragraphs: Friend, here's what Micah 6:1-8 is about. The LORD is not telling His people to go find a bigger offering. He opens with a question, "My people, what have I done to you?" and then reminds them of who He has been to them: the One who brought them up from Egypt and redeemed them from the house of slavery (Micah 6:3-4). His people had stopped remembering, and He wanted them to see His righteousness again (Micah 6:5).

Then the questions start piling up, and I know that feeling. "Should I come to Him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?" Then thousands of rams, then ten thousand rivers of oil (Micah 6:6-7). It's like trying to fix a mistake by baking MORE, MORE, MORE cookies when what you really needed to do was stop and ask what the person actually wanted. It sounds like the speaker is trying to buy peace with a bigger and bigger pile.

But look at the answer, and it's so simple it'll make you laugh. "He has shown you, O man, what is good. And what does the LORD require of you but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?" (Micah 6:8). That's the lesson, friend: He has already told us, and it's about how we live with Him and with people, not about how big our pile is. So when you're tempted to do something BIG to feel right with God, come back to this verse and take the next small step: act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with Him.
